sections.title: The permission for catalog artwork
paragraphs: UltraClipart gives you a non-exclusive, non-transferable permission to download, edit and incorporate its catalog illustrations into personal and noncommercial educational projects, subject to this page. There is no download fee or account requirement for that permission. You receive permission to use the material, rather than ownership of its underlying rights.

This covers the UltraClipart material we are entitled to license. A depicted brand, character, product, person or other protected subject may carry separate rights. A file being downloadable does not establish that every intended use is cleared. Statutory exceptions and rights that cannot lawfully be limited remain available.

sections.title: Teaching, schools and shared activities
paragraphs: A teacher can use catalog artwork in an ordinary noncommercial lesson, classroom handout or student activity, including when teaching is their employment. Share the completed educational resource with the learners who need it; do not distribute an editable collection of the underlying clipart for unrelated reuse.

Paid downloadable lessons, sale of resource packs, commercial training materials, school advertising and other revenue-linked uses are not automatically covered simply because they involve education. If the purpose is mixed or unclear, describe it to us before using the artwork. An institution’s own permissions and safeguarding duties also continue to apply.

sections.title: Redistribution, resale and misleading claims
paragraphs: Do not sell, sublicense, rent or redistribute the catalog artwork as stock media, standalone files, clipart packs, templates for resale or a competing image library. Do not give others a broader license than you received. A crop, recolor, traced version, composite or new file format remains subject to the permission for the catalog material it contains.

Do not claim that you created the unchanged catalog illustration or that UltraClipart or a depicted rights holder endorses your project. Do not register catalog material as your exclusive logo or trademark, or present it as exclusive work. Do not remove a notice required by a separately licensed component.

These restrictions describe our license grant. They do not eliminate lawful quotation, fair use, fair dealing or another statutory exception where the applicable law actually permits your particular use.

sections.title: Credit and ownership
paragraphs: The standard catalog permission does not require a visible UltraClipart credit in every permitted personal or educational project. A link to the original artwork page is welcome when practical. Keep the artwork URL or license page with your project records so you can identify the source later.

Optional catalog credit does not replace a notice required by a font, third-party icon or other separately licensed asset. This license does not assign copyright, guarantee exclusive ownership, or promise that every element qualifies for protection in every country.

sections.title: Studio projects, imports and starter designs
paragraphs: Original text, drawings and compositions you create on a blank Studio canvas remain yours to the extent you hold rights in them. UltraClipart does not take ownership of that original contribution merely because you used the editor. Imported files remain subject to their existing permissions; you are responsible for having the right to use them.

When a project includes catalog illustrations or a catalog-based starter design, the catalog conditions continue to apply to those parts. Your original additions do not become UltraClipart property, and your additions do not remove the source artwork’s restrictions. Saving a project or exporting a PDF does not change that distinction.

sections.title: Icons, fonts and other third-party materials
paragraphs: The Studio library includes Tabler Icons under the MIT License. Those icons retain the permissions and notice requirements of their own license; the catalog’s noncommercial restriction does not replace the MIT terms. The preserved icon notices identify the source. Other software and fonts likewise retain their own applicable licenses.

A third-party asset’s license does not grant rights in any unrelated catalog artwork used beside it. Keep required notices when distributing an editable asset or a substantial copy, and check the relevant license when moving source assets into another product.

sections.title: Images requested in AI Clipart Builder
paragraphs: Builder outputs are separate from the catalog permission. UltraClipart does not claim ownership of your original prompts or apply the catalog’s personal-and-educational restriction merely because an image was requested through the Builder. This is not a promise that an output is unique, copyrightable, exclusive, non-infringing or commercially cleared.

The current image service uses FLUX.1 schnell, whose model license is Apache 2.0. Prompt assistance is Built with Llama under the Llama 3.1 Community License. Model licenses govern the models and relevant uses; they are not a blanket clearance of every output. Cloudflare service terms and third-party copyright, trademark, privacy and personality rights can also apply.

Review the result and its intended use before publication. An output combined with catalog illustrations still carries the catalog conditions on those illustrations. The public sharing tool does not grant recipients a new reuse license.

sections.title: Ask about a particular project
paragraphs: Email ultraclipart@gmail.com with the artwork URL, your project, whether it is paid or promotional, the intended audience, and how the finished work will be distributed. Include any brand or character involved. Please ask before starting a use outside the standard permission.

An unanswered message is not permission. Any exception needs an explicit written agreement describing its scope; it does not automatically clear third-party rights. No general commercial license is sold or granted by this page.

sections.title: Keeping a record and resolving a breach
paragraphs: Keep a copy of the permission that applied when you obtained a file. A later page edit does not automatically rewrite a separately agreed permission or remove rights already granted under applicable law. Technical corrections or removal of an artwork do not create additional reuse rights.

If you discover that your use falls outside this permission, stop distributing the affected material and contact us about correction or an appropriate authorization. Any termination or remedy remains subject to applicable law and mandatory consumer protections.

sections.title: Who this notice covers
paragraphs: This notice describes UltraClipart’s website, catalog, Studio, Builder and public-link features. UltraClipart is the name used for the service in this notice. Send privacy questions and requests to ultraclipart@gmail.com.

You can browse and download without creating an account. Some features need ordinary hosting requests, browser storage or protected online processing. Local editing and public publication are different actions: opening a project does not automatically make it public. This notice concerns the current implementation, not a promise about every external app you may use with a downloaded image.

The report-preparation helper on the Copyright page builds a draft in this browser. It does not send the typed text to us by itself. If you open the email action or copy and send the draft, your email app and providers handle that message.

sections.title: Studio, Favorites and device storage
paragraphs: Studio processes imported files, drawings and edits locally. Favorites, boards, private notes, tags, project stages, pins, board covers, display preferences, favorite elements, palettes and recoverable project state use browser storage where available. That does not make the browser a guaranteed backup. Private browsing, storage pressure, a reset, another user of the profile or clearing site data can remove or expose locally saved work.

Save a project file if you need an editable copy you control, and export a Favorites backup before clearing data you want to keep. Downloaded files are independent of site storage and remain on your device until you remove them. We cannot remotely recover a local project that was never uploaded.

Local search uses public catalog data. Search text submitted in a page URL can still be visible in that URL, browser history and ordinary hosting requests. Do not enter private information in search fields, filenames or project titles.

sections.title: Builder requests and recent results
paragraphs: When you choose Generate, your description and selected settings are sent to Cloudflare Workers AI. The service prepares and checks the description with Llama 3.1 and requests an image with FLUX.1 schnell. Turnstile may process browser and connection signals to verify the request. This online step is different from editing a canvas locally.

The application’s usage ledger stores job status, timing, model and cost information with daily HMAC-based visitor and network identifiers. These identifiers are pseudonymous security data, not a promise of anonymity. The ledger does not store prompt text, generated image bytes or raw IP addresses. Our application does not automatically publish results.

Cloudflare’s current standard-inference policy says it does not use customer content to train models and limits input/output retention to service delivery, with specified safety, security and legal exceptions. Operational metadata may be retained separately. Provider processing is governed by its terms; our local-history controls do not erase provider records.

Do not put passwords, medical details, contact information, identifiable student records or other sensitive personal information into a prompt. A model may change or misunderstand a description. Free-capacity checks and content protections can reject a request; contact us if you believe a restriction is mistaken.

sections.title: Publishing, sharing and removing a link
paragraphs: Catalog sharing normally passes the original artwork page URL. Creating a public link for your own finished artwork is a separate, explicit publication action. It uploads a resized WebP image and its title, with dimensions and security/publication metadata, to Cloudflare D1. The editable project, layers and Builder prompt are not included in that public image.

Anyone with a public link can view, download or forward its image. The link is not an access-controlled classroom space or a private message. Do not publish identifying information about another person without the required permission. Choosing a social platform opens or sends data to that platform; we do not automatically post to your account.

A removal key is kept in your browser when available. Back it up if you may need to remove a publication from another device. Removal stops serving the image and title here, but cannot recall recipient downloads, screenshots, social previews or other third-party copies. If you lose a key or report someone else’s publication, email the share URL and enough information for us to assess the request.

sections.title: Why information is processed
paragraphs: Hosting requests deliver the pages and files you ask for. Browser storage enables requested conveniences such as recovery and Favorites. Protected online requests provide generation or publication and prevent misuse of limited resources. Contact details let us answer the message or rights request you send.

Where applicable data-protection law requires a legal basis, requested service processing may be necessary to provide that service or take requested steps; security and service administration may rely on legitimate interests balanced against your rights; mandatory retention or disclosure may rely on a legal obligation. Any future optional purpose that requires consent needs its own valid choice before activation.

You do not have to provide a prompt, publish an image or send an email to browse the catalog. Without the information and verification needed for a chosen online feature, that feature may not work. Our usage checks may automatically limit access to a free feature; we do not use them to make decisions about credit, employment or comparable legal entitlements.

sections.title: Service providers and international processing
paragraphs: Cloudflare provides hosting, content delivery, security, generation and application storage. Google provides the Gmail mailbox used for correspondence and the Google Forms contact form. Opening the embedded contact form connects your browser to Google; messages submitted through it are stored in the UltraClipart form and used to handle the request. Google processes form requests under its own privacy policy. Email messages remain in the mailbox and are not automatically added to the form. Apps, social platforms and email providers you choose also process the information you give them under their own policies. We do not add advertising trackers or third-party analytics, or sell personal information or share it for cross-context behavioral advertising.

Requests and correspondence may be processed in countries other than yours, including through global provider infrastructure. Cloudflare’s published data-processing terms describe mechanisms such as standard contractual clauses for relevant restricted transfers. The mechanism applicable to a particular transfer depends on the law and service terms involved; contact us for information about the relevant processing and safeguards. This notice does not promise that all processing stays in one country.

We may need to disclose information to comply with a valid legal requirement or address a substantiated security or rights concern. We limit such handling to what is relevant. A privacy notice is not a claim that a provider has no separate obligations or records.

sections.title: Cookies, settings and tracking choices
paragraphs: The current site uses necessary cookies for requested protected features, security and remembering the cookie notice. Both Accept Cookies and Necessary Only keep advertising and analytics disabled. The initial notice is shown outside the United States, or when the edge-provided country is unknown; settings remain available to everyone.

The region check uses Cloudflare’s approximate connection-country result, not device GPS, and does not build a stored country profile. A saved notice choice is not consent to a future advertising or analytics purpose. Blocking security cookies may prevent protected generation or publication.

Cookie Settings does not delete Favorites, projects, Builder history or removal keys. Use the appropriate feature controls for those records. Clearing all browser site data can delete them together, so save any work you need first.

sections.title: Your choices and privacy rights
paragraphs: Depending on the law that applies and the processing involved, you may have rights to access, correct or erase personal information; restrict processing; obtain portable data; and object to processing based on legitimate interests. Where processing relies on consent, you can withdraw it without changing the lawfulness of earlier processing. You can also complain to the relevant supervisory authority.

Email ultraclipart@gmail.com with “Privacy request”, the feature or URL involved and what you want us to do. We may need proportionate verification to avoid giving someone else access to your information. Do not send identity documents or a private project unless we explain why they are necessary. We do not require an account just to receive a privacy request.

We answer valid requests within the deadline required by the applicable law, explaining any lawful extension or exception. Some lawfully retained records may be needed for security, a legal obligation or a dispute. We cannot identify or retrieve browser-only records that were never sent to us; you control those through the device.

Where relevant law applies, you may contact your local EU/EEA authority, the UK Information Commissioner or the Turkish data-protection authority. California rights and authorized-agent procedures apply where the relevant law covers the service and request. Exercising a valid privacy right is not a reason for unlawful discrimination.

sections.title: Children, classrooms and sensitive information
paragraphs: Teachers and parents can use downloads to prepare activities without sending learner information. The site does not ask for a child’s name, school, class list or date of birth to download artwork. Avoid putting identifiable learner data into online generation, public images, titles or messages.

An adult should oversee a child’s use of protected online and public-sharing features and make sure any legally required permission is in place. A classroom context does not automatically authorize uploading a child’s information or make a public link private. The site is not represented as a school records system or a certified replacement for a school’s data arrangements.

If you believe a child’s personal information has reached us or appears in a shared image, email the relevant URL or description. We can review the concern and take appropriate action, including removal where required. Do not send extra sensitive information in the initial report.

sections.title: Security, updates and contact
paragraphs: We use bounded feature storage, signed protected sessions, verified publication requests and security controls appropriate to the service. No website or browser storage can be promised completely secure. Protect your device, keep project backups and report a suspected exposure with the affected URL.

We update this notice when the service’s processing changes and identify its review date. A page edit or an old cookie choice does not supply consent for an unrelated new purpose. For questions about this notice, the relevant records or an update, contact ultraclipart@gmail.com.

sections.title: The service and these terms
paragraphs: UltraClipart provides an illustration catalog, download tools, a browser-based Studio, AI Clipart Builder and optional public-link publication. These terms explain the conditions on which we provide those features. The Artwork License describes permission for catalog material; the Privacy and Cookie policies explain information handling.

Read the terms relevant to the feature you use, especially before uploading or publishing material. Nothing on this page claims that merely opening a page waives a statutory right or supplies consent to unrelated data processing. Questions about the service can be sent to ultraclipart@gmail.com.

sections.title: Responsible use of the site
paragraphs: Use the service lawfully, respect other people’s rights and do not interfere with its operation. Do not attempt unauthorized access, introduce malicious code, bypass verification, evade usage or storage limits, impersonate another person, or use public links to distribute unlawful, abusive or infringing content.

Use automated access only in ways permitted by applicable law and our published access instructions. Do not present catalog content as your exclusive stock library or use extraction to avoid the Artwork License. This does not remove a statutory exception or another right that the law does not allow us to restrict.

Adults supervising a child or class should check material, protect personal information and oversee online generation and sharing. Availability of school-themed artwork is not a guarantee that every result or public submission is suitable for every learner.

sections.title: Catalog artwork and your projects
paragraphs: Catalog downloads are provided under the free personal and noncommercial educational permission on the License page. Commercial use, sale of catalog-based merchandise and redistribution as a clipart library are not authorized by the standard permission. A modified file keeps the conditions on the material it contains.

You retain rights you hold in your own imported files, text, drawings and original additions. Using Studio does not transfer those rights to UltraClipart. You must have the permissions needed for an import or a publication, including any third-party copyright, trademark, privacy or personality rights.

Third-party icons, software, fonts and model-related materials keep their own licenses. A depicted brand or fictional character is not an endorsement or an additional rights grant. A public link, download button or successful export does not itself establish clearance.

sections.title: Local editing, recovery and exports
paragraphs: Studio editing and imported projects are processed in the browser unless you explicitly choose an online publication feature. Browser recovery is a convenience, not a guarantee of permanent storage or cross-device synchronization. Keep a downloaded project file when you need an editable backup.

Check the finished image, dimensions, text and print settings before relying on an export. Image-only content, source resolution, the chosen fonts and the printer’s workflow can affect the result. A CMYK PDF is not a guarantee of exact printed colors, print-shop acceptance or an accessible tagged PDF.

Do not treat a completed download as proof that a file meets every professional production requirement. The format guide and print-size calculator help with practical choices, but your intended use may need a printer’s proof or specialist review.

sections.title: AI Clipart Builder
paragraphs: Generation is an online service provided through Cloudflare, subject to model availability, verification, resource capacity and visitor, network and service-wide limits. The current interface shows availability. Limits can be reached sooner on a shared network. There is no automatic paid fallback or promise of a particular number of successful results.

A request already sent for processing may consume available capacity even if you close the page, cancel waiting, receive a timeout or dislike the result. We do not automatically retry an image request in a way that silently uses more generation capacity.

Outputs can contain errors in spelling, anatomy, counting, cultural details or resemblance to protected material. Check them before use. Do not request exploitation, abuse, hateful targeting, unlawful threats, impersonation, rights infringement or misuse of sensitive personal information, and do not bypass safeguards. Automated checks can be wrong; report a mistaken block or harmful result.

The current service uses FLUX.1 schnell for images and Llama 3.1 for prompt assistance. Prompt assistance is Built with Llama under the Llama 3.1 Community License. Applicable provider/model terms remain relevant. We do not guarantee an output’s originality, uniqueness, copyrightability, exclusivity or fitness for commercial use.

sections.title: Public links and the permission to host them
paragraphs: Creating a public link is your affirmative instruction to upload and publish the finished image and title. You give UltraClipart a non-exclusive permission to store, technically adapt, reproduce and display that submitted image as needed to provide the requested link and its download/preview. This permission does not transfer ownership of your original work.

The hosting permission lasts for the publication’s operation, subject to removal and any lawful residual handling described in Privacy. It does not authorize UltraClipart to sell your original project as stock artwork. Recipients do not gain a new reuse license merely from possession of a link.

Publish only material you are entitled to share. Keep your removal key or its backup. Public links are not private classrooms, permanent archives or substitutes for a project backup. Removal cannot retrieve copies already downloaded or held by third parties. Contact us with a share URL if you lose your key or need to report someone else’s publication.

sections.title: Availability, changes and moderation
paragraphs: We may maintain, change, limit or pause a feature or remove content for technical, security, legal or substantiated rights reasons. We may restrict misuse and review reports. Where the law requires an explanation, notice, appeal or another safeguard, those requirements continue to apply.

We do not promise uninterrupted access, a fixed release schedule, permanent public-link hosting, search-engine rankings or universal compatibility with every device or application. If one online feature is unavailable, locally loaded editing or previously downloaded files may still be usable, but offline operation depends on having the necessary code and assets.

A restriction may also arise from a shared-network limit or an automated verification error rather than misconduct. Email the affected URL, feature and brief details if you believe a decision is mistaken. Never include a secret removal key or password in a public report.

sections.title: Warranties, responsibility and mandatory rights
paragraphs: Please use reasonable care: review source permissions, keep backups and inspect work before publication or printing. We do not promise that every file is error-free or suitable for every purpose. Any exclusion or limitation of a warranty or responsibility applies only to the extent the relevant law permits.

Nothing here excludes liability that cannot lawfully be excluded, or takes away mandatory consumer, privacy or accessibility protections. A free feature is not a reason to disregard rights that apply to the relationship. We do not impose a blanket waiver, a mandatory arbitration clause or an invented foreign court on this page.

The law and courts with jurisdiction over a dispute remain determined by applicable rules, including mandatory protections for consumers. You can contact us first to try to resolve a problem; that does not remove an available right to seek a regulator’s or court’s help.

sections.title: Changes, existing permissions and contact
paragraphs: We identify the review date of these terms and update the page when the service changes. A change does not automatically amend a separately agreed permission or retroactively cancel rights already validly granted. Where notice or consent is legally necessary for a change, a silent page edit does not replace it.

If a provision cannot be enforced, its treatment is governed by applicable law; we do not use that circumstance to expand an invalid restriction. For questions, a correction or a proposed use outside the standard permission, email ultraclipart@gmail.com.

sections.title: What our rights statement covers
paragraphs: UltraClipart develops and maintains this website, its editorial material, design system, catalog organization and the materials it is entitled to provide. We reserve the rights we hold in protectable contributions, subject to the permission on the Artwork License page and the rights of other owners.

A copyright notice does not prove that every element qualifies for copyright or that all rights in a depicted subject belong to UltraClipart. Protection depends on the material, the contribution and the applicable law. We do not promise exclusivity, registration or universal ownership for every downloadable image.

The site’s selection, arrangement, written descriptions, code and visual design can involve rights separate from an individual file. Conversely, an idea, factual identification or a public-domain element does not become exclusively ours merely because it appears on this site. Statutory exceptions are not removed by this notice.

sections.title: Brands, people and protected subjects
paragraphs: Some illustrations refer to recognizable products, cultural subjects, entertainment characters or other protected material. Names and visual references help identify what is depicted. They do not state that the owner commissioned, approved or endorsed UltraClipart or your proposed use.

An editorial or personal context is not automatically a legal defense for every depiction. Commercial promotion, product packaging, merchandising, logos and potentially misleading associations can raise additional issues. Our standard catalog permission cannot grant a third party’s trademark, character, publicity or privacy rights.

Please report a wrong product identification, a concept presented as a released product, a misleading affiliation, or an inaccurate cultural detail. A faithful title should reflect the evidence for the actual image rather than an attractive but unsupported model name.

sections.title: How to report a copyright or other rights concern
paragraphs: Email ultraclipart@gmail.com with the exact artwork or public-share URL. A screenshot or search phrase alone may not identify the file reliably, so include the page address whenever possible. Say whether the concern is copyright, trademark, likeness/privacy, a misleading claim or another issue.

Give enough information to locate the material and understand your relationship to the rights: for example, that you created the work, hold the relevant rights or are authorized to represent the owner. Include a link to the original work or other relevant evidence and explain what action you request.

Do not send passwords, private project files, removal keys or identity documents in an initial report. We may request limited additional information if it is necessary to verify authority or resolve a genuine ambiguity. A clear factual report is more useful than unrelated personal information.
bullets: The exact UltraClipart page, file or shared-image URL.
The original work or other right affected, with a source link where possible.
Your name or organization and the capacity in which you are reporting.
A contact email and a specific explanation of the issue.
The correction, removal or clarification you are asking for.
An honest statement that the information you provide is accurate to the best of your knowledge.

sections.title: What happens after a report
paragraphs: We review the identified material, its available source and publication records, and the explanation and evidence supplied. We may ask a focused follow-up, correct a title or description, limit access while checking a credible concern, or remove an affected file or public link where appropriate.

An acknowledgment is not a final decision about ownership or a promise that a report has been accepted. A correction may be appropriate even when a complete removal is not. We aim to handle reports fairly and with the urgency the circumstances and applicable law require; we do not invent a fixed response or restoration deadline for every type of report.

Our review is an operational response, not a court’s determination of a disputed right. If your situation requires a formal statutory notice, counter-notice or another legal procedure, the relevant legal requirements apply. This email channel is not a claim that we have registered a particular statutory agent or qualified for every legal safe harbor.

sections.title: If your publication was restricted by mistake
paragraphs: Reply through ultraclipart@gmail.com with the affected URL, an explanation of the mistake and evidence of your permission or rights. Tell us how the material was created or obtained when that is relevant. Do not republish the same disputed material through another link to bypass review.

We consider a supported correction request and any legal obligations before deciding whether a restriction should change. A disagreement alone does not establish permission; equally, a report alone is not proof that your material infringes. Where a formal legal process applies, an informal email does not replace its required elements.

sections.title: Privacy and safety in reports
paragraphs: A report can contain personal information about both the reporter and another person. We use it to assess the issue, communicate about it and keep a necessary record of the response. Information may need to be shared with an affected party, service provider or competent authority when appropriate or legally required; we cannot promise absolute confidentiality.

Ask before including a sensitive document, a child’s details or information about someone who is not involved in the concern. If a public image exposes private information, say that clearly and identify the URL without repeating more of the private data than necessary.

sections.title: Factual, cultural and technical corrections
paragraphs: Not every problem is a copyright dispute. Tell us about an incorrect model or generation, an invented technical claim, a cultural or religious error, missing attribution, a misleading download description, a broken file or an accessibility barrier. Use the same email channel and explain the specific detail that needs attention.

For a factual identification, a reliable primary reference is helpful. We prefer a supported family-level label to an unsupported exact model. Speculative machines and imagined products should be identified as concepts. Correcting a source image may require its title, alt text, description, previews and file records to be reviewed together.

sections.title: Removal, saved copies and your responsibilities
paragraphs: Removing a page or public-link image stops the relevant serving on our service, but cannot retrieve copies saved by visitors or instantly erase social previews, search caches or third-party reposts. We can address what the service controls and consider relevant follow-up information.

If you previously downloaded affected material, reassess the intended use and any rights concern rather than assuming an old download guarantees clearance. If you see UltraClipart material redistributed outside the standard permission, send the original artwork URL and the location of the suspected reuse; we will assess the specific circumstances.

Please report in good faith. Knowingly false ownership claims or misleading reports can harm another person’s lawful work and may have legal consequences. Honest uncertainty is welcome: explain what you know and what you would like checked.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.description: Practical access information for UltraClipart, keyboard help, known limitations, testing scope and a direct way to report an accessibility barrier.
accessibility.intro: Useful access information, honest limitations and a direct way to ask for help.
highlights: WCAG 2.2 AA is our design and review target
Keyboard controls accompany visual tools
Tell us the task you need to complete

sections.title: Our approach and current status
paragraphs: We want UltraClipart to be usable by people with different vision, movement, reading and interaction needs. WCAG 2.2 Level AA guides our work on page structure, contrast, visible focus, labels, responsive layouts and controls. This is a target and a review framework, not a statement that every part of the site has been proven conformant.

We have not established full-site conformance through an independent accessibility audit and do not claim an accessibility certification. Automated results and browser checks cover particular pages and tasks; they cannot establish every screen-reader, motor, cognitive or real-device experience.

sections.title: Reading, browsing and finding artwork
paragraphs: Use the page headings and main navigation to move around the site. The skip-to-content link provides a shorter route past repeated navigation. Catalog images have descriptive alternatives, while purely decorative illustrations should not add unnecessary spoken content.

Search can find illustrations, subjects, collections, guides and tools. Suggestions are real links. Use Up/Down and Enter to select a suggestion, Escape to dismiss it, or the ordinary search button to open the full results page. Search results also provide filters and page controls.

Use your browser’s text size and zoom settings for comfortable reading. On narrow screens, navigation is available through Menu and longer controls wrap. If zoom or an assistive technology causes content or a control to become unreachable, report the affected page and the task.

sections.title: Keyboard help for Studio
paragraphs: The editor provides named buttons, a layer list, numeric properties, undo/redo actions and a download dialog alongside direct manipulation of the canvas. Selecting through Layers and editing numeric values can be easier than dragging an object.

The shortcuts below apply when focus is in the editor workspace and you are not typing in an input. Browser and assistive-technology shortcuts can take priority. A locked layer or another active tool can also affect an action.

rows: Tab / Shift+Tab
Move between reachable interactive controls
Follow the visible focus indicator; native dialogs contain their controls.
Enter / Space
Activate a focused button or native disclosure
The appropriate key depends on the control.
Ctrl+Z / Command+Z
Undo the latest edit
Use the named Undo button if your browser intercepts the shortcut.
Ctrl+Shift+Z / Command+Shift+Z
Redo an edit
A Redo button is also available.
Arrow keys
Move selected, unlocked objects
Shift uses a larger step; in pan mode the keys scroll the stage instead.
Delete / Backspace
Remove selected objects
Does not replace normal text editing when an input has focus.
Escape
Cancel an unfinished gesture or clear selection
In an open native dialog, Escape closes the dialog.
Layers and numeric properties
Select, position, size and rotate objects
These provide alternatives to precise pointer dragging for supported operations.

sections.title: Limitations to be aware of
paragraphs: A visual drawing canvas is not equivalent to a fully structured text document. Freehand drawing, pixel-level region selection, visual composition and some advanced tools may be difficult or unavailable to a person working entirely nonvisually. The available layer and numeric controls do not establish that every canvas operation has a complete assistive-technology alternative.

Artwork files may contain lettering or other information as pixels or shapes. A WebP image and a print-oriented PDF do not automatically carry the same text alternatives, reading order or document structure as the web page. We do not certify exported PDFs as PDF/UA or promise that text inside an illustration can be read by a screen reader.

User-published images and external applications can have accessibility limitations beyond the site’s page controls. Protected online features also depend on browser storage and third-party verification. If those protections prevent a task, ask us about the specific barrier rather than sharing a verification token or private file.

For a more text-based explanation of a workflow, start with the Guides and format help. If that does not meet your need, tell us the result you are trying to achieve so we can consider a useful alternative.

sections.title: What our checks can and cannot show
paragraphs: Our review includes responsive browser interaction, keyboard and focus behavior, form labels and automated accessibility checks on selected workflows. Recent search checks used Chromium and WebKit browser profiles at desktop and narrow widths, including 1440, 390 and 320 CSS pixels. These are sample-based results, not a whole-site audit.

A browser-engine profile is not a physical iPhone test or a substitute for testing with a person’s screen reader. Firefox could not be launched in the local environment used for those recent checks, so it was not counted as a pass. We use findings to prioritize improvements and welcome reports of combinations our checks have not covered.

sections.title: Report a barrier or request help
paragraphs: Email ultraclipart@gmail.com with the page URL, the task you were trying to complete and what prevented it. If useful, include your browser, device, zoom level and assistive technology/version. A short step-by-step example is usually enough; screenshots are optional.

Tell us if you need the explanation in another accessible form and what would help. We review reports and consider a correction or practical alternative. We do not promise a fixed turnaround for every issue, and you do not need to disclose a diagnosis or send sensitive personal information to ask for assistance.

sections.title: How this statement is maintained
paragraphs: This statement describes our current approach and limitations. We review it when relevant tools or access findings change and show its review date. Mandatory rights and any legal accessibility duties that apply are not reduced by this statement.
The W3C’s accessibility-statement guidance informs this page’s practical focus: the target, known barriers, available help and the scope of testing.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Clear answers about UltraClipart search, downloads, printing, Studio projects, Favorites, Builder, public links, privacy and artwork permissions.
faq.intro: Find a practical answer, then go straight to the tool or guide you need.
highlights: Browse by task or search the answers
Separate file, project and publication advice
Direct links to the relevant tools and policies

questions.question: Is UltraClipart free, and do I need an account?
answer: Catalog downloads and Studio are available without creating an account. The standard catalog permission is for personal and noncommercial educational projects. Free access does not authorize commercial use or resale. Builder and public-link features also have capacity and security limits.

questions.question: What can search find?
answer: Search covers published illustrations as well as subjects, collections, guides, site information and public Studio tools or starter material. Describe the visible subject and the details that matter, such as “red cardinal with holly” or “father holding newborn baby”. Use filters when you need a particular style, color, format, orientation or background.

questions.question: How do search suggestions work on my phone?
answer: Tap the suggestion’s name or thumbnail to open its page. An exact subject may lead to that subject’s collection, while a specific scene can lead directly to an artwork. Choose See all results or the search button to use the full results page. Keyboard users can select with arrow keys and Enter.

questions.question: Why do I see related results or no exact match?
answer: An image must match the requested details and active filters. Where related results are available, they are separated from complete matches and identify missing terms. Try removing an unnecessary detail or filter, or use a supported synonym. A result is not relabeled to pretend it contains something it does not.

questions.question: Where can I see new illustrations or all subjects?
answer: Recently Added shows actual new catalog entries. Categories lists available subjects and collections; a subject appears when publishable material is available. Counts come from the current published catalog rather than a promised production target.

questions.question: Should I choose Image, PDF or a project file?
answer: Image downloads provide the artwork’s WebP image for compatible digital apps. PDF is intended for a print layout; inspect its paper size, dimensions and stated profile. A saved Studio project keeps editable document information and serves a different purpose from either finished export.

questions.question: What opens when I choose Image or PDF on a catalog card?
answer: The download panel opens over the page so you can inspect the original file’s details and download it. Closing the panel returns you to the current page. The artwork page also contains file and print information. Downloads should use the actual original or the document you edited, rather than an unrelated substitute.

questions.question: Will the downloaded image have a transparent background?
answer: Check the particular artwork’s background and file details. Transparency is an alpha-channel property, not proof supplied by a white preview. A PDF uses a page and print layout. If you add a canvas background or start with an opaque imported image, your edited export may not be transparent.

questions.question: How large can I print an image?
answer: Use its actual pixel dimensions and the intended print density. Enlarging raster artwork does not create new detail. The print-size calculator helps convert dimensions; it cannot promise that a particular printer, paper or enlargement will look acceptable.

questions.question: Why do print colors differ from the screen?
answer: A lit screen and printed ink have different color ranges. Paper, the printer, its profile and the application’s color management can all change the result. Review the file information and ask the print provider for a proof when color matters.

questions.question: A download is not opening. What should I try?
answer: Check that the download finished and the app supports that format. Try the other supported format when appropriate. For a broken site download, email the artwork URL, format, browser and the steps you took. Avoid clearing all site data as a first response, because that can delete saved work.

questions.question: Can I make a design from a blank canvas?
answer: Yes. Open Clipart Studio to start blank or use an available starter composition. You can add text, supported shapes, vectors and artwork, organize layers and export a finished image or PDF. Imported material and catalog assets keep their own permissions.

questions.question: Can every illustration be separated into editable vector parts?
answer: No. Many catalog images are raster artwork and initially open as one image layer. Vector objects and text have different editing capabilities. A tool that extracts a raster region does not reconstruct a complete layered source illustration.

questions.question: How can I change one part of an image?
answer: Use Smart Select and the relevant region controls for supported raster work, or select an independent text/vector object through Layers. Inspect edges and the result, and use Undo if the selection is unsuitable. The available operation depends on the selected layer and whether it is locked.

questions.question: How do I keep a project editable or move it to another device?
answer: Use Save project to download an editable project file, then load that file on the other device. Finished Image/PDF exports do not preserve the same editable document information. Browser recovery alone is not cross-device synchronization.

questions.question: Can I recover work after closing the tab?
answer: Studio may retain recoverable work in this browser when storage is available. It is not a permanent backup. Private browsing, resets, browser storage eviction, clearing site data or using a different browser profile can make that work unavailable. Save a project file before an important session ends.

questions.question: Does Studio work offline?
answer: Some editing and exporting can work after the required code and assets are loaded. New catalog requests, protected generation, public publication and other network actions still need a connection. We do not promise that a page first opened offline will contain everything it needs.

questions.question: Where are my Favorites and boards saved?
answer: They are stored in the current browser when local storage is available. Boards can include organization and notes. They are not an account-based cloud library and do not automatically appear on another device.

questions.question: How can I protect my saved Favorites?
answer: Use the Favorites backup/export controls before changing devices or clearing browser data. Keep the downloaded backup somewhere you control and use the import/restore feature when needed.

questions.question: Will Necessary Only or Cookie Settings delete my work?
answer: No. Cookie notice choices do not clear Favorites, boards, projects, Builder history or public-link removal keys. Clearing all site data through the browser is different and can remove those records.

questions.question: Can someone using my computer see local work?
answer: Someone who uses the same browser profile may be able to view locally saved material. Use appropriate device/profile controls, avoid sensitive information in titles and prompts, and remove local records you do not want to leave on a shared device.

questions.question: What is sent online when I use the Builder?
answer: When you choose Generate, the description and settings go through the site to Cloudflare’s protected generation service. Prompt preparation and image generation are online operations. Ordinary Studio editing is local unless you explicitly publish a finished image.

questions.question: Why is generation unavailable or limited?
answer: The service has visitor, shared-network and service-wide capacity limits and verification safeguards. A school or shared connection can reach a network limit before an individual expects. Follow the current message and retry time rather than bypassing protections. No paid fallback starts automatically.

questions.question: Can a failed or canceled request use capacity?
answer: Yes. A request that has already reached model processing can consume available capacity even if you close the page, time out or dislike the result. A canceled wait does not necessarily cancel work already running remotely.

questions.question: Are Builder results guaranteed to match the description?
answer: No. Check counting, text, anatomy, cultural details and other requested constraints. Use ordinary editable text when exact wording matters. Background removal also needs inspection; it is not a guarantee of perfect edges or separation.

questions.question: What happens to recent generated images?
answer: When available, this browser keeps a bounded history of up to twelve results for seven days, with cleanup when the feature is used. Opening a result in Studio uses a short-lived local transfer. Download a project or finished file if you need your own lasting copy.

questions.question: Can I use a Builder result commercially?
answer: The catalog’s noncommercial permission is not automatically applied just because the result came from the Builder, but that is not a commercial clearance. Check provider/model terms, the result’s content and any copyright, trademark, privacy or personality rights. Combining it with catalog artwork keeps the catalog conditions on that material.

questions.question: Does sharing automatically post to my accounts?
answer: No. Catalog sharing passes the artwork URL, and device/social sharing uses the destination you choose. The receiving app or platform has its own terms. Creating a public artwork link on UltraClipart is a separate, explicit publication action.

questions.question: Is an UltraClipart public link private?
answer: No. Anyone who has the link can view, download or forward its image. Do not use it as a private classroom, confidential client proof or access-controlled file store. Your project layers and Builder prompt are not included in the finished public image.

questions.question: How do I remove a public link?
answer: Use its removal control and the removal key saved in your browser, or your backed-up key. If the key is lost, contact us with the share URL and relevant details for review. Never post the secret key in a public message.

questions.question: Can removal recall every copy?
answer: No. Removal stops the image being served through the relevant link here. It cannot retrieve a recipient’s download, screenshot or a social platform’s existing preview. Keep a separate backup of your own original work.

questions.question: Does a public link let another person reuse the image?
answer: Possession of a link is not a new reuse license. The creator’s rights and any source artwork restrictions still apply. Ask for the permission required for your intended use.

questions.question: Can I sell products or paid educational resources using catalog art?
answer: The standard catalog permission does not allow commercial use, paid resource downloads, print-on-demand merchandise, paid client work or redistribution as clipart. Ask for a specific written permission before a use outside personal and noncommercial educational projects.

questions.question: Does editing an illustration remove its license conditions?
answer: No. Recoloring, cropping, tracing, combining or changing the file format does not remove the source artwork’s conditions. Your original additions keep their own rights, while the catalog parts keep theirs.

questions.question: Is attribution required?
answer: The standard catalog permission does not require a visible credit in every permitted project, although a source link is welcome. Separately licensed assets, such as MIT-licensed icons, retain their own notice requirements.

questions.question: Are brands and characters officially licensed or endorsed?
answer: A depicted subject or identifying title does not establish endorsement, affiliation or permission from the relevant brand, character or product owner. Our license cannot grant rights we do not hold. Consider the intended use and report an inaccurate identification or misleading association.

questions.question: Does UltraClipart add advertising or analytics trackers?
answer: The current site does not add advertising trackers or third-party analytics. Necessary request delivery, security checks, optional online features and browser storage are still forms of processing described in the Privacy and Cookie policies.

questions.question: How do I request a correction or report a rights problem?
answer: Email ultraclipart@gmail.com with the exact page or share URL, the problem, relevant evidence and the action you request. If you represent a rights holder, explain that relationship. Do not send passwords, secret removal keys or unnecessary identity documents.

questions.question: What if a keyboard or assistive technology cannot complete my task?
answer: Report the page, intended task and barrier to ultraclipart@gmail.com. Browser, device, zoom and assistive-technology details can help. Our Accessibility page describes practical controls, testing scope and known limitations; it does not claim a full-site certification.

questions.question: How do I contact UltraClipart?
answer: Use ultraclipart@gmail.com. For a technical problem, include the page, browser and reproducible steps. For a license question, explain the planned purpose and distribution. Avoid including private student information or other sensitive material.

editorial-process.title: Our Editorial Process
editorial-process.description: See how UltraClipart selects subjects, reviews distinct illustrations, checks names and download files, and handles corrections after publication.
editorial-process.intro: How we choose subjects, review illustrations, and prepare the files you download.
highlights: A useful subject and a distinct composition
Descriptions that match the visible artwork
Matching previews, downloads, and editing sources

sections.title: Begin with a clear subject and a real use
paragraphs: A classroom label, a birthday card, and a printable activity need different kinds of illustrations. We start with the subject, the scene, and the way the artwork could be used. A clear brief gives the illustration a purpose before it becomes another item in the library.

We consider recognizable details, framing, expression, materials, and space around the subject. The aim is to offer useful choices within each collection, rather than repeat one image with a different color or crop.
bullets: A subject people can recognize and search for
A composition that works as an individual illustration
A useful place in an existing or carefully planned collection

sections.title: Make the composition meaningfully different
paragraphs: Variety comes from the whole illustration: its silhouette, viewpoint, arrangement, expression, and setting. For character collections, clothing and pose also matter. For objects and plants, their structure, presentation, and intended use help distinguish one composition from another.

We compare incoming work with published and planned artwork. File checks and image-similarity checks help flag repetition; visual review decides whether the difference is meaningful. A recolor, crop, repair, or alternate export belongs to the original artwork, not to a new count of independent designs.
bullets: Compare the overall composition, not just the filename
Keep repairs and revised exports with the same artwork
Do not treat a different file checksum as proof of originality

sections.title: Name what the illustration actually shows
paragraphs: The title should help you recognize the subject. Alternative text describes the visible artwork, while the description explains details that help you choose it for a project. These fields should agree with one another and with the image.

Recognizable vehicles, devices, and other branded subjects need extra care. We compare distinctive features with official manufacturer material when needed. If only a product family is supported, we use that family; filenames, colors, and logos alone do not establish an exact model, year, or specification. Imagined products are identified as concepts.
bullets: Use the same reviewed identity in the title, description, and image information
Avoid details that cannot be supported by the visible artwork
Reconsider the identification whenever the source image is replaced

sections.title: Look closely at the image itself
paragraphs: We look for awkward cropping, missing parts, unwanted marks, accidental lettering, and details that conflict with the description. Edges and transparent areas need attention against light and dark backgrounds, because a white thumbnail can hide a halo or an unfinished edge.

Botanical, cultural, religious, and technical subjects may need additional reference checks. An attractive illustration can still contain an incorrect detail. A repair should improve the affected artwork and its description without being counted as a separate original.
bullets: Check the complete shape and the smaller details
Review edges and transparency where relevant
Match visible details to the written description

sections.title: Prepare matching files for the same artwork
paragraphs: The preview, downloadable image, PDF, and editor source should all refer to the same illustration. Technical validation checks file signatures, dimensions, recorded sizes, and content hashes. A content hash acts as a digital fingerprint for a file. Transparency and paired files are checked where relevant. A filename extension alone does not prove the file format.

Small display previews help the site load efficiently. They do not replace the original download. PDFs provide a page layout for printing. Enlarging a fixed-resolution image cannot add detail, and a correct file does not guarantee an identical result on every printer.

links.label: Compare image, PDF and project formats

sections.title: Make the library easier to explore
paragraphs: Reviewed titles, descriptions, and visible characteristics support search and filtering. Related collections should lead to relevant, available subjects. Search aliases can help you find an image, but they do not change what the image depicts.

Black & White classification considers the actual artwork, rather than a filename or the color of the subject alone. Catalog totals come from eligible published entries. Drafts and withdrawn items should not appear as finished downloads, and uploading a file alone does not publish it.

sections.title: Check the experience around the download
paragraphs: Publication brings the illustration, its descriptions, and its approved files together. Source checks and build checks are followed by browser checks for tasks such as searching, opening an artwork, using download controls, and editing a project. Findings need to record what was actually tested.

Each check has a specific purpose. A file hash helps verify that the bytes match a recorded version; it does not judge the composition. An automated accessibility scan can find some barriers; it does not establish full accessibility. A successful build does not prove that every interaction works on every device.
bullets: Check links and download actions as well as the page appearance
Keep personal projects, Favorites, and preferences through ordinary updates
Review reported problems after publication

sections.title: Creative direction and technical care
paragraphs: UltraClipart co-founders Melih and Mustafa bring two complementary responsibilities to this process. Melih leads Design & Creative Direction; Mustafa leads Software & Infrastructure. Visual choices and technical delivery need to work together.

The editorial standard is the same across the library: a useful illustration, an accurate description and files that match. This page describes our process and review criteria; it is not a promise that every illustration is free of defects.

sections.title: Keep permissions clear
paragraphs: The artwork license explains the uses UltraClipart permits. Rights in third-party characters, brands, fonts, and imported materials may be separate. A depicted product name does not imply endorsement, and a technically valid file does not establish ownership of everything it depicts.

User-published links are separate from the reviewed catalog. Sharing a design does not automatically turn it into a catalog-approved illustration or create a new reuse license. Check the relevant permission before using artwork in a project.

sections.title: Help us improve an artwork or page
paragraphs: If something looks wrong, send the exact artwork or page link and explain what we should check. A useful report might identify an inaccurate name, a visible image defect, a broken download, or an accessibility barrier. For a factual identification, include an official reference when possible.

We can reassess the image and its descriptions, revise the affected files or restrict availability while reviewing a concern. A replacement image needs a fresh review of its descriptions and related files. We do not promise a fixed response time, but a specific report makes the problem easier to investigate.
bullets: The artwork or page URL
What seems incorrect, and what you expected
Your browser and reproduction steps for a technical problem
